findings.text: Bar use is a conditional use (C) in the NCT-Valencia zoning district per Planning Code §762, requiring Planning Commission approval through a Conditional Use Authorization hearing with 300-foot mailed notice and a 30-day appeal period.

The Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District (§249.60) permits restaurants to serve alcohol but requires a new or relocated bar use to transfer a liquor license from another bar within the SUD; a Type 42 bar license must be sourced from an existing bar in the Mission SUD, not purchased on the open market from outside the district.

In 2011, Planning approved a CUA at 991–999 Valencia (on the same parcel) to upgrade from Type 41 to Type 47 (full bar) for an existing full-service restaurant, demonstrating historical willingness to approve alcohol intensification at this address.

Two CUA applications for bar uses within 210 m (970–974 Valencia in 2010 and 2519 Mission in 2019) were withdrawn before hearings; the records do not state reasons, but withdrawals suggest applicants sometimes abandon the CUA process rather than face contested hearings or unmet SUD license-transfer requirements.

Only 3 dated use decisions for comparable concepts within 1,000 ft in the last 10 years (1 approved, 2 withdrawn), far too few to calculate a meaningful approval rate or predict the outcome of a discretionary CUA hearing at this address.

findings.text: ABC Type 42 (beer-and-wine bar) is a non-quota license, so ABC issues new licenses directly, but nearly every city treats Type 42 as a bar use requiring conditional-use approval before ABC will issue the license.

The Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD (§249.60) requires a new bar to use a license transferred from another bar within the SUD; confirm with ABC and a license broker whether a Type 42 license is available for transfer from an existing bar in the Mission SUD before proceeding.

Nine active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft and 51 within 1,000 ft place this address in an undue-concentration area; ABC will require a Public Convenience or Necessity (PCN) finding from the Planning Commission or Board of Supervisors, which adds 1–3 months and opens a second public-comment period beyond the CUA hearing.

An active Type 41 on-sale beer-and-wine license for Sarita's Grill & Beer was issued at 995 Valencia on November 3, 2023; the license is tied to the restaurant use and cannot be converted to a Type 42 bar license without a new ABC application and Planning CUA approval.

Neighboring 999 Valencia received CUA approval in July 2023 for a Type 20 off-sale license transfer under §249.60, with conditions including a 9 p.m. alcohol-sales cutoff and a three-year validity period; expect similar good-neighbor conditions (hours, lighting, signage limits per §202.2) for a Type 42 bar license at 995 Valencia.

The Entertainment Commission has approved POE permits on the immediate Valencia block at 998 Valencia (Amados, 31 m away) and at nearby Mission Street venues (Hidden Frequency at 2500 Mission, Arcana at 2512 Mission, Foreign Cinema at 2534 Mission, all within 150–172 m), demonstrating that POE permits paired with food and alcohol service are routinely approved on this corridor.

Planning approved an Entertainment Commission POE permit referral at 2500 Mission in July 2026, and agency referrals for EC permits are nearly always approved if the underlying use is permitted or conditionally permitted in the zoning district.

A recent nighttime-entertainment approval at 2500 Mission (145 m, July 2026) noted that the use is subject to the Entertainment Commission's Good Neighbor Policy; expect similar conditions (sound limits, neighbor contact, security plan) for a POE permit at 995 Valencia.

One Limited Live Performance permit accessory to a retail video store at 1034 Valencia (94 m) was disapproved by Planning in April 2015; the denial suggests that entertainment permits accessory to non-food uses or applications that do not meet primary-use thresholds face rejection, but a wine bar with live music as a secondary use is a stronger fit for POE approval.

findings.text: Any food facility with a kitchen requires DPH plan review of equipment, finishes, and menu ($828–$2,207 flat fee for 2026–27 depending on scope), a pre-opening inspection, and a Permit to Operate ($470 application fee, $0 annual license fee for restaurants for 2026–28 per the FY2026–27 fee schedule).

The address has operated as a full-service restaurant with on-file DPH approvals since at least 1999 (referrals in 1999, 2001, 2002, 2020); a change of operator or entity requires a new Permit to Operate, but the space's prior restaurant use and existing kitchen layout simplify plan review.

At least one certified food safety manager must be on staff within 60 days of opening (CalCode §113947.1), and all food employees must obtain a California Food Handler Card within 30 days of hire; these are training requirements, not discretionary permits.

Limited cooking (small plates, panini, no full fryers or grills) reduces the scope of exhaust-hood and fire-suppression requirements compared to a full commercial kitchen, but DPH will assign equipment and sanitation standards during plan check that must be met before the final inspection.

findings.text: Tenant improvements (kitchen build-out, bar, finishes, plumbing, electrical) require a DBI building permit with plans routed to DPH, Fire, and PUC; most over-the-counter permits are now filed through the PermitSF portal, and full plan review with interdepartmental routing takes 2–4 months.

The concept profile states the space was previously food/beverage (change_of_use = false); since the address has operated as a restaurant with a Type 41 license since at least 1999, the tenant improvements do not trigger Planning's change-of-use review or neighborhood notification under §311/312, shortening the building-permit timeline.

Limited cooking requires a commercial kitchen hood with fire suppression, grease interceptor, and SFPUC FOG program compliance; the FOG Installation Verification Form earns a 14.2% sewer-bill reduction, and an undersized or missing interceptor is a common reason DBI withholds final sign-off.

A building permit on file at 995 Valencia (2020-012158MIS) shows DPH approved the continuation of restaurant use in January 2021; if prior kitchen equipment (hood, sinks, flooring) remains and meets code, the scope and cost of tenant improvements will be lower than a ground-up kitchen build-out.

filing_playbook.action: Confirm Type 42 license availability and PCN requirement with ABC and a license broker; negotiate lease contingency on CUA and ABC approvals.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Contact ABC's San Francisco district office to request a LAMP report for the census tract and confirm whether a Type 42 license is available for transfer from another bar within the Mission Alcohol SUD. Engage a California liquor-license broker to identify available Type 42 licenses in the SUD and their transfer costs. Include a lease contingency requiring Planning CUA and ABC license-transfer approval within 12–18 months, and confirm the landlord will support the CUA and POE applications.

filing_playbook.action: Form the legal entity (LLC or corporation) and obtain an EIN, then register the business with the SF Treasurer and file a fictitious business name statement.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File LLC Articles of Organization with the California Secretary of State ($70) and obtain an EIN from the IRS (free, same day online). Within 30 days, register the business with the SF Office of the Treasurer & Tax Collector to obtain a Business Account Number (BAN); the BAN is required for all subsequent city permits. File a fictitious business name (DBA) statement with the SF County Clerk if the public-facing name differs from the legal entity name, and publish the statement in an approved newspaper for four weeks.

filing_playbook.action: File the Conditional Use Authorization application with SF Planning for the bar use, including the Mission Alcohol SUD §249.60 license-transfer requirement and good-neighbor commitments.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the CUA application to SF Planning with the BAN, lease or letter of intent, and a project narrative explaining that the wine bar will transfer a Type 42 license from another bar within the Mission Alcohol SUD per §249.60, will serve limited food (small plates) prepared in a limited kitchen, will host live music with amplified sound ending by 2 a.m., and will comply with good-neighbor conditions under §202.2 and the Mission SUD rules. Hold the required pre-application community meeting and incorporate neighbor feedback (e.g., soundproofing commitments, contact protocol) into the CUA application. Expect 6–10 months from filing to Commission hearing, including environmental review, 300-…

filing_playbook.action: In parallel with the CUA, commission an acoustic report and submit the DPH plan check for the limited kitchen and bar build-out.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Hire an acoustical engineer to measure existing sound transmission to neighboring residences and design soundproofing (windows, doors, wall treatment) to meet anticipated Entertainment Commission sound limits; submit the acoustic report with the POE application. Simultaneously, submit scaled drawings, equipment schedules, and a menu to DPH Environmental Health for plan review ($828–$2,207 flat fee); show hand sinks, three-compartment sinks, food-prep surfaces, refrigeration, limited cooking equipment (panini press, small oven), and grease-interceptor connection. DPH will assign a plan reviewer; book the pre-final and final inspections at least two weeks in advance.

filing_playbook.action: After the CUA is approved, file the Place of Entertainment permit application with the Entertainment Commission, including the acoustic report and the approved CUA motion.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Email the Entertainment Commission Deputy Director to confirm POE eligibility, then submit the POE application ($2,708 fee for 2026–27) with the lease, the approved CUA motion, the acoustic report, a security and crowd-management plan if the space will hold 50+ people, and a narrative committing to the Entertainment Commission's Good Neighbor Policy (complaint log, neighbor contact, sound monitoring). Post the yellow notice at the site for 30 days and notify neighbors within 300 feet. Expect a Commission hearing 2–4 months after filing; the Commission will likely condition the permit on sound limits (e.g., 75 dBA at the nearest residential window), operating hours (live music ending by 10 o…

filing_playbook.action: File the ABC Type 42 application with the approved CUA and a signed agreement to transfer a Type 42 license from another bar within the Mission SUD; request a Public Convenience or Necessity finding from Planning or the Board of Supervisors if required.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the ABC Type 42 application with the entity registration, seller's permit, lease, approved CUA motion, and a signed license-transfer agreement with the seller bar (the license must come from another bar in the Mission SUD per §249.60). Post the 30-day ABC notice at the premises. If ABC determines the census tract is undue-concentration, request a Public Convenience or Necessity finding from the Planning Commission or Board of Supervisors (typically a letter stating the use serves the public convenience and addresses an unmet need); this adds 1–3 months and requires a second round of neighbor notification. ABC will then process the transfer application (60–150 days if unprotested; lon…

filing_playbook.action: File the building permit for tenant improvements with DBI, routing through DPH, Fire, and PUC, and obtain the grease-interceptor approval from SFPUC.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the building-permit application through the PermitSF portal with architectural plans showing the bar layout, limited kitchen equipment, hand sinks, three-compartment sinks, exhaust hood and fire suppression, electrical and plumbing, ADA compliance, and emergency exits. Route the permit to DPH (health plan check), Fire (hood suppression, occupancy), and PUC (grease interceptor). SFPUC will assign a Discharger Category and specify the interceptor size; install it before the final inspection and submit the Installation Verification Form to earn a sewer-bill reduction. filing_playbook.action: Complete food-safety training, obtain workers' compensation insurance, register for payroll taxes, and apply for the Health Permit to Operate after the final building inspection.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: At least one owner or employee must pass an accredited food-safety manager exam (ServSafe, Prometric) within 60 days of opening; all food employees must obtain California Food Handler Cards within 30 days of hire. Purchase workers' compensation insurance from a licensed carrier or State Fund and register with the CA Employment Development Department for payroll taxes using the EIN. After the DBI final inspection, apply online for the DPH Permit to Operate ($470 application fee, $0 annual license fee for 2026–28) and schedule the final DPH inspection; the permit is issued after the inspector confirms the facility matches the approved plans and a certified food-safety manager is on staff.

timeline_cost.path: Conditional Use Authorization for bar use (6–10 months) + Place of Entertainment permit (2–4 months, in parallel with CUA appeal period) + ABC Type 42 transfer with Public Convenience or Necessity finding (4–6 months, overlapping CUA) + building permit and tenant improvements (3–5 months) = 10–18 m…
timeline_cost.notes: The critical path is the Conditional Use Authorization (6–10 months including pre-application meeting, environmental review, Commission hearing, and 30-day appeal period; $3,100–$15,000 fee depending on construction cost, with possible First Year Free fee waiver for new storefronts). The Place of Entertainment permit (2–4 months, $2,708 fee) can be filed after CUA approval and will run in parallel with the ABC application. ABC Type 42 transfer (4–6 months, $1,000–$1,600 fee) requires locating and purchasing a Type 42 license from another bar within the Mission Alcohol SUD (market price unknown; confirm with a broker) and obtaining a Public Convenience or Necessity finding from Planning or the Board if the census tract is undue-concentration (adds 1–3 months). Building permit and tenant improvements ($800–$15,000 fee based on construction valuation; 2–4 months plan review plus 1–3 months construction) can overlap the CUA and ABC processes. Health plan check ($828–$2,207) and Permit to Operate ($470 application, $0 annual fee for 2026–28) follow the building final. Minor permits: business registration ($55–$700), entity formation ($70–$150), fictitious business name ($60–$120), sign permit ($300–$1,500), seller's permit (free), EDD registration (free), RBS training ($3–$30 per person), food handler cards ($7–$15 per employee), food-safety manager certification ($100–$250), ASCAP and BMI licenses ($300–$2,500 each per year), and workers' comp insurance (percentage of payroll, not a government fee). Total government fees (excluding the Type 42 purchase price, construction costs, insurance premiums, and music licenses) range from roughly $8,500 to $26,000. The lease should include a 12–18 month contingency for CUA, POE, and ABC approvals, and the operator should budget an additional $50,000–$150,000 for a Type 42 license transfer within the Mission SUD (price to be confirmed with a broker). The biggest risk is the unavailability of a Type 42 license for transfer within the SUD; if no license is available, the concept must pivot to a restaurant with a Type 41 (which does not require CUA under §249.60 and is principally permitted in NCT-Valencia for restaurants) or abandon the bar-use classification.

records_summary: 995 Valencia St is in the NCT-Valencia district where bars require Conditional Use Authorization and sit inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District, which permits restaurants to serve alcohol but requires a new or relocated bar to use a license transferred from another bar within the SUD. The address has operated as a restaurant with a Type 41 license since at least 1999, most recently as Sarita's Grill & Beer (active Type 41 issued November 2023). The immediate block is saturated: 24 registered food/drink businesses and 9 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft, with 51 licenses within 1,000 ft—a density that will trigger ABC's Public Convenience or Necessity review. Only three comparable use decisions in the last 10 years within 1,000 ft (one approved, two withdrawn), far too few to show a meaningful approval rate.
